title: Capacity Decision Visualizer: Operator Manual and Runbook
author: Priya Kapoor
content:
Overview

This document describes the Capacity Decision Visualizer (CDV): an operational tool used by Redwood SRE to translate real-time SLO signals and capacity telemetry into human-readable decisions and automated remediation actions. The CDV combines SLO burn-rate signals, headroom forecasts, tenant priority, and recent incident context to provide: a) a visual risk dashboard, b) an evidence-backed decision lattice for throttles/preemptions, and c) an audit trail for incident reviews and error-budget reconciliations.

Goals and scope

- Goal: reduce time-to-decision during SLO stress periods and standardize capacity actions across on-call teams.
- Scope: model-serving and inference-facing platform services (hosted API, Dedicated paths, cluster-level autoscale). CDV is NOT the source of truth for billing metrics or long-term capacity procurement.

Key concepts and terminology

- SLO View: aggregated SLO performance window (1h, 6h, 24h) per service and per tenant class.
- Burn-rate Signal: computed rolling burn-rate with confidence intervals (95%).
- Headroom Forecast: probabilistic capacity prediction for N=1,3,12 hours using historical load profiles and current warm pools.
- Priority Lanes: tenant lanes (production/standard/trial) used for proportional throttling and booking.
- Decision Lattice: pre-authorized set of actions mapped to signal combinations (low/high burn, constrained headroom, critical tenant impact).

Ownership and SLAs

- Primary owner: eng-sre (Tooling subteam).
- Maintainer oncall: capacity-tooling@redwood.internal (pager duty rotation).
- Support SLA: triage acknowledged within 30 minutes during business hours, severity-1 within 10 minutes.

Data sources and telemetry (what the visualizer uses)

1) SLO and error-budget pipeline
   - Source: SLO Observability pipeline (kafka-topic: slo-events).
   - Measurements: latency_p50/p90/p99, availability%, request_count, error_count, burn_rate windows (1m, 5m, 1h).

2) Capacity & fleet signals
   - Source: cluster-capacity-metrics (Prometheus, metrics prefix: cluster_capacity_*).
   - Measurements: GPU_free_pct, warm_pool_size, model_warm_instances, OOM_events, avg_seq_len, queue_depth.

3) Tenant and quota metadata
   - Source: tenant-config-store (Vault-backed).
   - Measurements: tier, committed_throughput, reserved_capacity_id, eligible_for_eviction flag.

4) Incident context and recent rollouts
   - Source: incident-store and deployment-events (SRE-incident index). Includes active postmortem IDs and recent deployment hashes.

Visualizer UI walkthrough (operator-facing)

- Landing page: global heatmap of services by burn-rate and headroom risk. Hover to see causative signals.
- Service detail: timeline of SLO windows, stacked headroom forecast bands, top contributing tenants by request volume.
- Decision pane: shows the active Decision Lattice node recommended action, reason summary (evidence list), and required approvals.
- Audit lane: chronological actions taken (manual or automated) with operator notes and links to runbook sections used.

Decision lattice (summary table)

The Decision Lattice maps a small set of combinatorial inputs to actions. Operators should follow this lattice in order. The lattice is simplified below; full canonical table lives in the CDV config (see Configuration examples).

- Input: Burn-rate low (<1.2), Headroom high (>20%), Priority: any -> Action: Monitor, no intervention.
- Input: Burn-rate medium (1.2–3.0), Headroom low (5%–20%), Priority mixed -> Action: Activate light throttling on trial lane (5–15% reduction), start tenant contact.
- Input: Burn-rate high (>3.0), Headroom constrained (<5%), Critical tenants impacted -> Action: Execute proportional soft-eviction on non-critical lanes, enable burst-absorber pool, notify oncall leads.
- Input: Sustained breach (>=30min) with no headroom recovery -> Action: Escalate to SRE incident, open emergency capacity cutover, and activate tenancy fallback routes.

Runbook: step-by-step operator procedure

1) Validate telemetry: Confirm CDV data freshness (prometheus lag <30s, slo pipeline lag <45s). Commands:
   - kubectl -n observability exec -it prometheus-0 -- promtool check metrics
   - curl -sS https://internal-metrics/slo/health | jq .lag

2) Reproduce the signal: Use the service detail timeline to identify whether the burn is sustained or spike. Look at request_count and top tenants.

3) Map to lattice: Choose the Decision Lattice node that matches observed signals. Document the matching evidence IDs in the CDV action modal.

4) Execute approved action: For soft-throttle:
   - CDV UI: Select throttle template -> set percentage -> preview impact -> apply.
   - CLI: rdc capacity action apply --service <svc> --policy throttle --pct 10 --reason "CDV guided"

5) Observe 10-minute windows for effect. If no improvement, escalate following escalation matrix.

Automation and safety gates

- Safe mode: Automation is gated by the runbook and requires two conditions: a) median headroom forecast below configured threshold, and b) automated action quota not exceeded for the 24h window.
- Kill-switch: manual kill-switch available in CDV for immediate rollback of automated policies; only oncall lead or SRE director can permanently disable automation.

Incident handoff and post-incident evidence

- When an SLO incident is declared, snapshot the CDV audit lane and attach it to the incident ticket (incident-store id). The snapshot includes telemetry excerpts, decision trace, operator notes, and the config hashes of policies applied.
- Postmortem requirement: every incident must include a CDV-derived timeline and at least one candidate capacity remediation action that would have changed the outcome.

Retention, logging, and compliance

- Audit lane entries are retained for 13 months. Policy config changes are versioned and immutable once signed.
- Sensitive tenant identifiers are redacted in public postmortems; full audit remains in restricted storage (confidential).

Configuration table (key parameters)

| Parameter | Default | Purpose | Owner | Notes |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| headroom_alert_pct | "10%" | Threshold to move to high-risk lane | eng-sre | Configurable per cluster |
| auto_throttle_pct_limit | "20%" | Max automatic throttle percent | eng-sre | Can be tuned by service |
| automation_daily_quota | "3" | Max automated actions per service per 24h | eng-sre | Prevents runaway automation |
| burn_rate_window_minutes | "60" | Window for burn-rate calculation | observability | Should match SLO windows |

(See CDV config repo: git@internal:redwood/cdv-configs.git)

Example policies and CLI snippets

- Example policy JSON (CLI-friendly compressed):
  {"policy_name":"trial-throttle-template","max_pct":15,"apply_if":{"burn_rate">2.0,"headroom_pct"<10}}

- Common commands:
  - rdc capacity check --service inference-api --window 60m
  - rdc capacity simulate --policy trial-throttle-template --duration 10m
  - rdc capacity action preview --service <svc> --policy <name>

Training and rollout guidance

- Pilot: enable CDV in read-only mode for 4 teams for 6 weeks, collect operators’ feedback.
- Full rollout: require training session for oncall teams and update incident templates to include CDV snapshot step.

Operational metrics to monitor CDV health

- CDV UI latency (95th): <500ms.
- Data freshness: >99% of signals <45s lag.
- Automation false positive rate: target <5% (investigate every FP).

Troubleshooting checklist

- If headroom forecast is missing: verify batch job (forecast-runner) status and model availability.
- If SLO pipeline lag >1m: escalate to observability team and run slo-pipeline rebuild.
- If audit lane shows duplicate actions: check idempotency key generation in action runner.

Appendix: small change procedure for CDV policies

1) Author a policy change MR in cdv-configs. Include rationale, test plan, and a rollback plan.
2) Test in staging with rdc capacity simulate.
3) Request approvals from eng-sre owner and Product owner (if customer-impacting).
4) Deploy to canary cluster for 24h, observe no FP.
5) Promote to prod with annotated changelog.
